record.title: Prompt-injected agent writes unbounded, undeletable rows into the shared audit log via uncapped tool-call args
record.description: The agent token (lowest-trust principal, assumed prompt-injected) controls the free-form args dict of every tool call. service._call_tool writes an event=tool_request audit row with payload {"args": _logged_args(tool, args)} as its very first action, before policy.decide, so even denied or approval-requiring calls still persist the row. _logged_args only special-cases write_file content (replacing it with size+sha256); for every other tool and every other key the args pass through verbatim. No size cap exists at any layer: FastAPI/Starlette/uvicorn impose no default request-body limit, ToolCall.args is an unconstrained dict[str, Any], Settings has read/write/upload caps but no args/body cap, the shipped Caddy reverse_proxy has no request_body max_size, and audit.append serializes and INSERTs the payload with no size check. One request therefore persists an arbitrarily large row into the shared, append-only control-plane SQLite audit DB (a single DB for all sandboxes, on host disk). UPDATE/DELETE are blocked by triggers, so the operator cannot prune oversized rows without rebuilding the DB and destroying the hash chain. audit.verify() loads every row and rehashes each full payload, and /ui/verify calls audit.list(limit=100000), so one agent can permanently bloat the shared audit store and make the operator's own audit/verify tooling slow and memory-heavy for the life of the DB.
record.root_cause: _logged_args (service.py:131-137) returns agent args unchanged except write_file content, and _call_tool (service.py:297-298) persists them via audit.append before any policy decision; neither the HTTP layer (api.py:50-51,206-211), configuration (config.py:54-57), shipped proxy (deploy/Caddyfile:5) nor audit.append (audit.py:143-187) bounds the serialized payload; the append-only triggers (audit.py:35-38) make the oversized rows unrecoverable.
record.intended_behavior: Agent-supplied tool arguments recorded for audit are bounded in serialized size (as write_file content already is), so one lowest-trust request cannot persist an arbitrarily large, undeletable row into the shared audit DB or amplify the operator's verify/list path.

trace.description: Agent POSTs /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/{tool}; body.args is an unconstrained dict[str, Any] (api.py:50-51) passed straight to box.call_tool with actor=p.kind; no request-body or args size limit.

First action in the tool path: audit.append(event='tool_request', payload={'args': _logged_args(tool, args)}), executed before policy.decide (line 299), so the row persists even for calls that are later denied or sent to approval.

Static method returns the args dict unchanged for every tool except write_file; only write_file 'content' is replaced with content_bytes+content_sha256. All other keys/tools (e.g. a 3 MiB 'junk' value on read_file) pass through verbatim.
payload = self._mask(payload or {}); _mask recurses over the dict and json.dumps serializes it with no size check before the INSERT.
The full json.dumps(payload) is persisted into the append-only audit table; verify() (audit.py:208-233) and list(limit=100000) (web.py:270) later re-load and rehash every full row.

evidence.description: Only the write_file 'content' key is special-cased; every other tool/key is returned unchanged.
tool_request row appended as the first action, before policy.decide at line 299.
INSERT persists json.dumps(payload) with no size cap.
audit_no_update / audit_no_delete triggers (RAISE ABORT 'audit log is append-only') make oversized rows unprunable.
verify() selects all rows ORDER BY id and rehashes each full payload.
/ui/verify calls box.audit.list(sandbox_id=..., limit=100000), re-loading up to 100k full payloads.
Settings defines max_read_bytes/max_write_bytes/max_upload_bytes but no args/request-body cap.
Shipped behind-proxy deployment uses a bare 'reverse_proxy agentbox:8765' with no request_body max_size.
ToolCall.args: dict[str, Any] = {} is unconstrained; passed to box.call_tool (api.py:210) with no body limit.

conditions.description: Valid agent token for its own sandbox (lowest-trust network principal; threat model assumes a prompt-injected agent).
Each request appends one unprunable row sized to the body; recovery requires rebuilding the DB and losing the hash chain, since UPDATE/DELETE are trigger-blocked.
Both the default local serve and the shipped behind-proxy Caddy deployment lack a body cap; an operator-added body cap would reduce per-row magnitude but not cross-request accumulation.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent adds a large junk field to tool args it already controls; the control plane records the full args into the shared append-only audit DB permanently and re-reads them on every operator verify/list.
payloads: Repeat with list_dir, exec, key, type, etc. (any non-write_file tool, or any non-'content' key).
instructions: In the OS-enforced sandbox (sbx v08: /usr/bin/python3.13, /target read-only on sys.path, /scratch writable, no network, no Docker, uid 65534, 512 MiB, 1 CPU), reproduce service._logged_args verbatim and confirm a non-write_file args dict with a 3 MiB junk value is returned unchanged while write_file content is stripped.

Open agentbox.audit.AuditLog on a scratch DB and append actor='agent', event='tool_request', tool='read_file', payload={'args': logged_args(...)} with the 3 MiB junk; measure length(payload) of the stored row.
Append 3 more rows with junk; sum length(payload).
Attempt DELETE and UPDATE on a row; observe the append-only triggers.
execution.observed_result: logged_args kept the 3,145,728-byte junk key unchanged (write_file content was stripped); the stored row's payload was 3,145,774 bytes; 4 rows totalled 12,583,024 bytes; both DELETE and UPDATE raised sqlite3.IntegrityError 'audit log is append-only'; verify() returned ok=True after re-checking all 4 rows; list(limit=100000) returned all 4 rows with the full 3 MiB payload intact. Independently reproduced in sbx v08 (/scratch DB); see agents/v08/artifacts/repro_v08.out (consistent with the hunter's agents/h-buffer/artifacts/audit_cap.out).

remediation.strategy: Bound the serialized size of agent-supplied args before persistence: when the json-serialized args exceed a fixed limit, store a byte count + sha256 + truncated head (mirroring the existing write_file content handling), either in _logged_args or in a shared helper invoked by audit.append. Add a request-body/args size limit on the tool endpoint (and a request_body max_size in the shipped Caddyfile) as defense in depth.

likelihood.reason: The agent controls the args dict in normal operation; adding a large field is trivial with its own token and requires no special conditions.

impact.reason: Persistent, unprunable growth of the shared append-only audit DB (single DB for all sandboxes, on host disk) plus memory/CPU amplification on every operator verify()/ui-verify list(100000); recovery requires rebuilding the DB and losing the hash chain. Not RCE or a guaranteed crash.

confidence.reason: Every layer read from source: uncapped pass-through in _logged_args, pre-decision persistence, absence of any HTTP/config/proxy/audit body or row cap, append-only triggers, and full re-read in verify/list all confirmed. Uncapped persistence, trigger-blocked DELETE/UPDATE, and full re-read independently reproduced in the sandbox (repro_v08.out).
